topic: What trade-offs exist between using fully metallic transmitarrays versus dielectric-based designs in terms of orbital thermal management and mass constraints?
consensus_response: The choice between fully metallic transmitarrays and dielectric-based designs depends on the specific requirements of the satellite application. Fully metallic cells offer simplicity but suffer from increased unit cell loss (~2 dB) due to slot length limitations, affecting maximum beam deviation and capacity. Dielectric-based designs reduce unit cell loss but introduce complexity and potential dielectric losses, impacting system capacity and interference susceptibility. However, they offer improved thermal management capabilities, allowing for more efficient heat dissipation and enhanced system reliability in orbital environments.
reference_context: The reference context highlights the challenges of designing high-performance, compact transmitarray antennas for satellite applications while managing thermal issues and minimizing mass. It provides data on average unit cell loss, spillover loss, and measured peak gain for both fully metallic and dielectric-based designs.
